concept.overview: Sonatype Nexus Repository is a repository manager: a central server that stores, organizes, and serves the binary artifacts and dependencies your software depends on and produces. It hosts your own build outputs (JARs, npm packages, Docker images), proxies and caches packages from public registries (Maven Central, npmjs, Docker Hub), and groups both behind a single URL. It sits between your CI/CD pipeline and the outside world as the source of truth for binaries.
concept.whyItMatters: Builds should not pull straight from the public internet every time — it is slow, flaky, and a supply-chain risk. A repository manager gives you fast local caching, reproducible builds, a private place to publish internal artifacts, and a control point for security policies and cleanup. Nexus is one of the two dominant repository managers (with JFrog Artifactory) and a common part of enterprise pipelines.
useCases: Hosting internal build artifacts (Maven, npm, NuGet, PyPI) privately
Proxying and caching public registries to speed up and stabilize builds
Serving as a private Docker registry for container images
Providing reproducible dependencies decoupled from public uptime
Enforcing cleanup and retention policies to control storage growth
concept.architecture: Nexus organizes storage into repositories of three kinds. A hosted repository stores artifacts you publish (your internal releases and snapshots). A proxy repository caches artifacts fetched on demand from a remote (e.g., Maven Central); the first request pulls and stores them, later requests serve the cache. A group repository aggregates several hosted and proxy repos behind one URL, so clients configure a single endpoint. Artifacts live in a blob store on disk (or cloud storage), while metadata lives in Nexus's database. CI tools and developers authenticate and pull dependencies from a group URL and publish outputs to hosted repos; cleanup policies prune old snapshots to reclaim space.

definitions.def: A server that stores and serves binary artifacts and proxies external registries.
A repo that stores artifacts you publish (internal releases/snapshots).
A repo that caches artifacts fetched from a remote registry on demand.
An aggregate of hosted and proxy repos exposed under one URL.
The on-disk (or cloud) storage backing repository content.
The package type a repo serves: maven2, npm, docker, pypi, nuget, etc.
Rules that delete old/unused artifacts to control storage.

bestPractices: Point all builds at a group URL so you have one endpoint and a single cache.
Use proxy repos for public registries to speed builds and reduce external dependence.
Publish releases and snapshots to separate hosted repos with clear retention.
Apply cleanup policies so storage doesn't grow without bound.
Back up blob stores and the database, and secure repos with authentication/roles.
pitfalls: Letting builds pull directly from the internet, causing slow, flaky, unreproducible builds.
No cleanup policy, so snapshots fill the disk over time.
Mixing releases and snapshots in one repo, breaking reproducibility.
Anonymous write access, allowing anyone to publish artifacts.
Forgetting to back up blob stores — losing every stored artifact.

Maven mirror in settings.xml routes all traffic through Nexus
Separate release vs snapshot hosted repos
Cleanup policies + blob store backups keep it healthy
Nexus can be a private Docker registry too

quiz.question: What is Nexus Repository primarily used for?
options: Storing and serving binary artifacts and proxying registries
quiz.explanation: Nexus is a repository manager for binaries and dependencies.

quiz.question: Which repository type caches artifacts from a remote registry?
quiz.explanation: A proxy repo fetches from a remote on demand and caches the result.

quiz.question: What does a group repository do?
options: Aggregates hosted and proxy repos behind one URL
quiz.explanation: A group exposes multiple repos through a single endpoint for clients.

quiz.question: Proxying public registries makes builds faster and more reproducible.
quiz.explanation: Caching reduces external calls and shields builds from public registry outages.

quiz.question: Where does Nexus store the actual artifact content?
quiz.explanation: Content lives in blob stores; metadata lives in the database.

quiz.question: Your Nexus disk keeps filling with old snapshot builds. Best fix?
options: Configure a cleanup policy to prune old artifacts
quiz.explanation: Cleanup policies automatically remove old/unused artifacts to reclaim space.

quiz.question: Nexus can act as a private Docker registry.
quiz.explanation: Nexus supports the docker format for hosting and proxying images.

quiz.question: Why should builds point at a group URL instead of many separate repos?
options: One endpoint plus a single cache simplifies client config
quiz.explanation: A group gives clients a single URL that aggregates hosted and proxy repos.

quiz.question: Anyone on the network can publish artifacts to your hosted repo. What's wrong?
options: Anonymous write access should be disabled; require auth/roles
The blob store is too big
quiz.explanation: Write access must be authenticated and role-controlled to protect the supply chain.

quiz.question: Releases and snapshots should generally be stored...
options: In separate hosted repos with clear retention
quiz.explanation: Separating them keeps releases immutable/reproducible and snapshots prunable.

tasks.title: Stand up Nexus and browse repos
tasks.goal: Run Nexus and explore its default repositories.
steps: Start Nexus (container or install) and log in
Explore the default hosted, proxy, and group repos
Identify the format of each (maven, npm, etc.)
Find the URL clients would use for the group
successCriteria: Nexus is reachable and you can log in
You can name the three repository types present

tasks.title: Proxy a public registry
tasks.goal: Speed up and stabilize dependency resolution.
steps: Create a proxy repo for a public registry (e.g., npm or Maven Central)
Add it to a group repository
Point a client (npm/mvn) at the group URL
Install a dependency and confirm it is cached in Nexus
successCriteria: A second install is served from the cache

tasks.title: Publish internal artifacts
steps: Create hosted repos for releases and snapshots
Configure your build tool with credentials to deploy
Publish an artifact from a CI job
Verify another project can consume it from the group
successCriteria: The artifact appears in the hosted repo
A consumer resolves it via the group URL

tasks.title: Harden and maintain the repository
steps: Add roles/users and disable anonymous write
Set up blob store and database backups
Use it as a private Docker registry for a pipeline image
successCriteria: Old snapshots are pruned and backups are configured
